evals.prompt: En evals/inputs/carriers cada vez que añadimos un transportista tengo que tocar shipping.ts, eta.ts y labels.ts. Aplica el patrón Strategy.
evals.expected_output: States the problem (a switch repeated in 3 files, 3 stateless variants) and picks the simplest solution that fits: a table/registry of rules per carrier (or a lightweight Strategy) in a single place. The three switches disappear and the three files delegate or are consolidated; adding a carrier becomes one entry. Original tests green and public API intact. Justifies why a table instead of a class hierarchy + factory, and when to reassess. The reply is in Spanish.
assertions: shippingCost, etaDays and carrierLabel are still exported with their signatures
The carrier names ('express', 'pickup') are defined in a single rules file, not in three
No class hierarchies or factories per carrier are created
The reply explains why it picks a table or lightweight Strategy over classes + factory

evals.prompt: I want a serious pattern for the configuration in evals/inputs/app-config: apply Singleton and Factory to it.
evals.expected_output: Challenges the request with arguments: loadConfig is already a pure function with an injectable, testable environment; a Singleton adds global state and makes testing harder, and a Factory has no variants to create. Leaves the design as it is, or at most proposes loading the configuration once at the composition root and passing it as a parameter. Does not introduce getInstance or Factory classes. Tests green.
assertions: No Singleton (getInstance, static instance or similar) appears in the code
loadConfig is still exported with an optional environment parameter
The reply explains why Singleton and Factory don't fit here and offers an alternative

evals.prompt: En evals/inputs/notifier quiero poder cambiar de proveedor de email y probar notifyShipped sin llamar al SDK real. ¿Qué patrón uso? Aplícalo.
evals.expected_output: Identifies Adapter (port and adapter / DIP): defines a domain interface (e.g. EmailSender with to, subject, html) and an adapter that wraps MailClient; notifyShipped receives the port as a parameter or through the constructor and no longer imports the SDK. A test uses an in-memory fake without touching vendor/mail-sdk. The only file that imports the SDK is the adapter. The interface uses domain language and does not copy the SDK's fields (recipient/title/htmlBody). SDK errors do not leak. Existing tests green, or adapted and declared. The reply is in Spanish.
assertions: notifier.ts no longer imports the SDK (vendor/mail-sdk.ts)
There is a single file outside vendor/ that imports the SDK (the adapter)
There is a notifyShipped test that uses an in-memory fake without importing the SDK
The reply names the Adapter or port-and-adapter pattern and justifies it with the problem
